answer: Agents gain influence only after locking a slashable stake and earning endorsements from established peers. If a newcomer is exposed as a Sybil, a fraud proof slashes its stake and part of the endorsers’ stake, sending a ripple through the trust path. This makes cheap mass registration ineffective: an attacker must tie up capital, persuade liable agents to vouch, and risk losing both deposits and reputation. Hiding identities across a meadow or ridge does not avoid that cost.
